body.heading: Meet the herbs
paragraphs: Herbs are plants we grow for their smell and flavour. Ask your adult to show you some safe ones — mint, basil, rosemary, and lavender are friendly starters.
Rub a leaf gently between your fingers and smell. Rubbing wakes up the smell hidden inside the leaf.

body.heading: Describe the smells
paragraphs: Mint smells cool and fresh, like toothpaste. Rosemary smells woody, like a pine forest. Basil smells sweet and peppery at the same time.
Every herb has its own smell signature. Chefs choose herbs the way artists choose colours.

body.heading: Draw a smell
paragraphs: Draw a picture of each herb and write the words its smell gives you. You are making a smell map of the garden, made by your nose.
Your nose can tell thousands of smells apart. Gardeners and cooks train theirs every day, one leaf at a time.

takeaway: Herbs hide strong smells in their leaves, and a gentle rub lets your nose read them like labels.
materials: Herb plants in pots (an adult chooses)
safetyNotes: Only smell plants an adult names as safe herbs. Never taste or eat any plant unless an adult says it is safe food and prepares it.
screenFreeExtension: Close your eyes and play the smell-guessing game with herb leaves your adult hands you.
